dish: Okinawan 'okazu' plate (five vegetables and island tofu), tebichi simmered two days, hirayāchi, taco rice
n: Taishū Shokudō Mickey, Park Avenue (大衆食堂ミッキー)
w: A decades-old one-woman shokudō on Koza's Park Avenue carrying on her mother's recipes; OTV Okitive profiled its never-shared 'secret' family flavour, and KozaWeb lists it among Koza's taco-rice and A-sign-era diners. The okazu plate of five vegetables and island tofu is the house signature.

dish: Teppanyaki tenderloin steak cooked at the table, with shrimp cocktail (the 1970 three-item menu)
n: Sam's Anchor Inn Ginowan (サムズアンカーイン 宜野湾店)
w: The founding branch of Okinawa's Sam's steak chain, opened on Route 58 in Mashiki in August 1970 by American Ray Payne; its then-novel teppanyaki show and original menu of shrimp cocktail and tenderloin made it a pre-reversion steak institution. The Ryukyu Shimpo marked the chain's 55th anniversary in 2025.

dish: Okinawa soba in a clear broth; limited-quantity Kin-Agu pork-bone soba
w: A small soba shop near the Enobi crossroads that the Ryukyu Shimpo's gourmet column praised for a simple, deeply flavoured bowl drawing soba fans from across the island; OTV Okitive featured its limited-quantity bone-broth soba made with Kin-Agu pork. Closes when sold out.

dish: Yūbaru soba set with sanmai-niku pork belly and Shirikawa tofu
n: Subaya Yūbaru Menkata, Uruma (すば家 ゆーばる麺方)
w: A family soba house opened in July 2025 by the min'yō singer Kamiya Chihiro's family under their Tsuken-jima house name, carrying on the 'Yūbaru soba' served at the family's Tsuken Island minshuku. The Okinawa Times and OTV Okitive both featured its local-produce set meals with sanmai-niku and Shirikawa tofu.

dish: Natural-yeast shokupan (white loaf) from Hokkaido 'Harutaka blend' flour; scones
n: Ippe Coppe, Minatogawa Stateside Town (ippe coppe いっぺこっぺ)
w: A natural-yeast bakery in a converted 1950s–60s American military house in Urasoe's Minatogawa Stateside Town, specialising in additive-free shokupan made from Hokkaido 'Harutaka' flour; Tabirai and Mapple both single it out and Urasoe's own tourism site lists it. Opens 12:30 and closes when sold out.
